response.title: My front and back lawns are separated by a driveway and a gate. Can one wire-free robot mower do both by itself?
response.answer:
Yes. One wire-free robotic lawn mower can mow both your front and back lawns automatically, even if they're separated by a driveway and a gate.

However, there's an important distinction: being able to mow two separate lawns doesn't necessarily mean the robot can travel between them without your help.

You'll need a mower with three capabilities:

Multi-zone mapping: It can recognize your front and back lawns as separate mowing areas.

Automatic zone transitions: It can travel between the two lawns using a mapped route, including crossing a driveway.

Gate access: It can physically pass through the gate without you opening it manually.

How it would work
Illustrative layout: the mower follows a programmed route through an accessible gate to reach another lawn. Your actual layout may differ.

The mower can finish one zone, navigate to the other, mow it, and return to its charging station—provided the entire route is accessible and supported by that model.

Also check that the driveway crossing is relatively level, doesn't involve a high curb, and doesn't expose the mower to unsafe vehicle traffic.
